standard_prerequisites.name: The map from the henselization to the completion of a Noetherian local ring is flat and injective
standard_prerequisites.use: Sets up the minimal prime comparison.

standard_prerequisites.name: Flat maps satisfy going down and injective ring maps realize every minimal prime of the target as lying over one from the source
The completion is henselian and the number of branches is defined via minimal primes of henselizations
The strict henselization of the completion is the base change of the strict henselization over the henselization
standard_prerequisites.use: Enables repeating the argument for part (3).

core_obligations: Part (1): by the henselization-noetherian lemma the map A^h -> A^wedge is flat and injective; going down for flat maps and the injective minimal-prime lemma give that every minimal prime of A^h is hit, i.e. the induced map on minimal primes is surjective (proof lines 31949-31953).

Part (2): the number of branches is defined via minimal primes over the henselization; since A^wedge is henselian by the complete-henselian lemma and the map on minimal primes is surjective, the branch count of A is at most that of A^wedge (proof lines 31953-31956).

Part (3): by the henselization-noetherian lemma (A^wedge)^{sh} = A^{sh} tensor_{A^h} A^wedge, so the same flat injective argument with A^{sh} -> (A^wedge)^{sh} proves the geometric branch inequality (proof lines 31957-31960).
proof_roadmap: Establish flatness and injectivity of A^h -> A^wedge and prove the minimal-prime surjection (proof lines 31949-31953).
Deduce the branch count inequality from the definitions and henselianness (proof lines 31953-31956).
Repeat via the strict henselization base change for geometric branches (proof lines 31957-31960).
